questions.q: What were the people of Tyre saying against Jerusalem?
questions.a: The people of Tyre were saying they would be filled up as Jerusalem was ruined.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to Tyre?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would raise up many nations against Tyre, who would destroy its walls and towers.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would be done at the place Tyre once stood?
questions.a: Yahweh said that nets would be dried out at the place Tyre once stood.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say he was bringing against Tyre?
questions.a: Yahweh said he was bringing Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, against Tyre.

questions.q: How did Yahweh say the walls of Tyre would be broken down?
questions.a: Yahweh said the walls of Tyre would be broken down with Nebuchadnezzar’s battering rams.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh say the stone and wood of Tyre’s houses would be laid?
questions.a: Yahweh said the stone and wood of Tyre’s houses would be laid in the midst of the waters.

questions.q: What will the chiefs of the sea do when the terrible slaughter occurs in Tyre?
questions.a: The chiefs of the sea will come down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, strip off their colorful clothing, and sit on the ground trembling.

questions.q: Where do the chiefs of the sea lament that the famous city of Tyre is now?
questions.a: The chiefs of the sea lament that the famous city of Tyre is now in the sea.

questions.q: To where did Yahweh say the people of Tyre would be brought down?
questions.a: Yahweh said the people of Tyre would be brought down into the pit.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, when would Tyre be found again?
questions.a: According to Yahweh, Tyre would never be found ever again.

commentary.text: Ezek. 26:1-14 To be secretly pleased with the death or decay of others, when we are likely to get by it; or with their fall, when we may thrive upon it, is a sin that easily besets us, yet is not thought so bad as really it is. But it comes from a selfish, covetous principle, and from that love of the world as our happiness, which the love of God expressly forbids. He often blasts the projects of those who would raise themselves on the ruin of others. The maxims most current in the trading world, are directly opposed to the law of God. But he will show himself against the money-loving, selfish traders, whose hearts, like those of Tyre, are hardened by the love of riches. Men have little cause to glory in things which stir up the envy and rapacity of others, and which are continually shifting from one to another; and in getting, keeping, and spending which, men provoke that God whose wrath turns joyous cities into ruinous heaps.

Ezek. 26:15-21 See how high, how great Tyre had been. See how low Tyre is made. The fall of others should awaken us out of security. Every discovery of the fulfilment of a Scripture prophecy, is like a miracle to confirm our faith. All that is earthly is vanity and vexation. Those who now have the most established prosperity, will soon be out of sight and forgotten.
